To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

misonidazole (a hypoxic radiosensitizer) potentiates cyclophosphamides and other cytotoxic drugs, whether assayed for cell survival or tumourgrowth delay, and that the optimum effect is seen when it is given one hour before the drug.

the radiosensitizer misonidazole (RSU 1069) potentiates, in vitro, the cytotoxicity of cyclophos-phamide and melphalan, and that it also inhibits recovery from potentially lethal damage caused by cyclophos- phamide in the WHF fibrosarcoma.

the radiosensitizer misonidazole (Misodazole) potentiates both the action of cyclosphosphamide (Cyclosphosphamide) and recovery from potentially lethal damage induced by this drug in a mouse fibrosarcoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the radiosensitizers misonidazole and SR-2508 in combination with cytotoxic drugs in the treatment of cancer.
the development of combined modality treatment for the management of cancer.
the use of radiosensitizers in the treatment of solid tumours.
